html:
A merchant republic based on the city of Dubrovnik, called Ragusa in Italian, on the Dalmatian coast of present-day Croatia. It ran its own affairs from 1358, when it threw off Venetian rule, until Napoleon's armies ended it in 1808.

Dubrovnik had been under Venetian rule since 1205. In 1358, by the Treaty of Zadar, it passed under the loose overlordship of the king of Hungary. Later it paid tribute to the Ottoman Empire in return for protection and trading rights inland.

Ragusa lived by trade. Its ships carried goods between the Ottoman Balkans and Italy. A council of nobles ruled, with a rector who changed every month so that no one man could gain too much power. It banned the slave trade in 1416, and in 1377 set up one of the first quarantines against plague.

Its motto was "Liberty is not sold for all the gold in the world". Napoleon's forces occupied it in 1806 and abolished the republic two years later.
